Use my code INVICTA for a exclusive welcome package (for new users only). Comment what you won! Enjoy
We continue our coverage of the financial history of ancient Rome. In past episodes we explore the topics of currency, banking, and inflation. Now we turn our attention to the businesses of ancient Rome. This begins with an overview of the economic landscape of antiquity. We then look at how people organized for business using various forms of collective action. At the lowest level this meant the household unit of the Familia. Beyond this were the Clientela which functioned as large networks of Patrons and their clients. Then finally we get into the more organized structures of the collegia, societies, and publicani.
Sources: “The societas publicanorum and corporate personality in Roman private law” by Geoffrey Poitras and Frederick Willeboordse (https://www.sfu.ca/~poitras/Roman.pdf) "Competition between Public and Private Revenues in Roman Social and Political History (200–49 BC)" by James Tan “Collegia, Stability and the Vox Populi” by Steven Umbrello “Justinian. The Digest of Roman Law” by Penguin Classics “The Letters of the Younger Pliny” by Penguin Classics “Roman Ostia” by Russell Meiggs

entry.title: True Size of the Battle of Cannae (FULL DOCUMENTARY)

media:group.media:title: True Size of the Battle of Cannae (FULL DOCUMENTARY)
media:group.media:description:
All parts of our 3D simulation of the True Size of Cannae in Unreal Engine 5. Support the channel on Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/InvictaHistory and check out our cool mugs and maps on the store: https://invicta-history-shop.fourthwall.com/
In this history documentary series we will be bringing to life the True Size of the Battle of Cannae between Rome and Carthage in the midst of the Second Punic War. The simulations were made possible thanks to Unreal Engine 5 and the support of Dr. Adrian Goldsworthy.
We begin with a review of the Roman and Carthaginian Army sizes. Next we turn to the site of battle to identify where they would have been placed. As the armies now enter the battlefield we model the camps which were erected in the days leading up to battle. Finally we arrive at the climactic day of August 2nd with the Battle of Cannae. Here we cover the army deployments and formations from both a bird's eye view and the boots on the ground. In our next episode we shall turn to the unfolding of the battle itself.

entry.title: True Size - French Army of the Hundred Years War (1337-1453) DOCUMENTARY

media:group.media:title: True Size - French Army of the Hundred Years War (1337-1453) DOCUMENTARY
media:group.media:description:
Watch the full documentary on Joan of Arc (and more) with HistoryAdventures https://youtube.com/@HistoryAdventures-1?si=9Gnw0pkHq-MzyltD
In this history documentary we explore the True Size of the Army of Joan of Arc. This involves a review of the nature of the French Army as it entered the Hundred Years War. We cover its method of organization, equipment, and muster. The major phases of the war are then covered to highlight the changes to the military of medieval france. This includes casualties from battles like Crecy and Agincourt as well as the broader cullings of the Black Death. We then review the nature of the army of 1430 when Joan of Arc emerged to lead it. The documentary then covers the early campaigns of the maiden which culminates in the Siege of Orleans.
